title: 7.4 Properties of Special Parallelograms

icans: I can tell whether a statement about rhombuses, rectangles, and squares is always, sometimes, or never true.
I can use the diagonals of rhombuses and rectangles to find measures.
I can decide whether a quadrilateral in the coordinate plane is a rectangle, rhombus, or square.

vocab: a ________________ with four congruent sides and four right angles

blocks.p: Family tree. Write quadrilateral, parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus, and square in the boxes.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Rhombus: A rhombus is a parallelogram with four _______________.
Rectangle: A rectangle is a parallelogram with four _______________.
Square: A square is a parallelogram with four _______________ and four _______________.

blocks.stem:
Decide whether each statement is always, sometimes, or never true.
a.  A rectangle is a square.
b.  A square is a rhombus.
c.  A rhombus has congruent diagonals.

notes: Rhombus Diagonals and Opposite Angles Theorems: The diagonals of a rhombus are _______________, and each diagonal _______________ a pair of opposite angles.
titles: Rhombus Diagonals and Opposite Angles Theorems

blocks.stem: ABCD is a rhombus with diagonals meeting at E, and m∠ABC = 70°. Find m∠ABD and m∠AEB.

notes: Rectangle Diagonals Theorem: The diagonals of a rectangle are _______________.

blocks.stem: In rectangle ABCD, AC = 4x − 3 and BD = 2x + 9. Find x and AC.
Decide whether the parallelogram with vertices (−2, 1), (1, 3), (4, 1), and (1, −1) is a rectangle, rhombus, or square. Explain.
In rhombus JKLM, JK = 3x + 5 and KL = 5x − 7. Find x and the length of each side.
In rectangle JKLM, JL = 5y − 8 and KM = 3y + 6. Find y and JL.
